intent: Bring setup_midnight_shutdown.sh (1734 lines) under the 250-line cap — the last file over it — without changing a byte of the five scripts it generates into /usr/local/bin.
scope: New libs: ms_guard, ms_config_guard, ms_scripts, ms_override_mgr, ms_monitor, ms_units, ms_report, ms_setup_flow
Non-goal: running `setup`. It installs systemd units, chattr +i's the config and arms a shutdown timer.
changes: All 20 real top-level functions moved into eight libs. The prompt's '~39 functions' count included definitions that only LOOK top-level: log(), now_epoch(), cmd_add() and friends appear at column 0 because they are inside heredocs that generate standalone scripts. The brace-matching extractor keeps each heredoc inside its owning function, so those moved as part of their generator rather than being treated as separate functions.

create_config_guard's 224-line quoted heredoc became a verbatim payload file, the same convention already used for lib/payloads/night-lockdown-*.sh.in. It was the last thing keeping a lib over the cap.
$_MS_PAYLOAD_DIR is defined in the same file as its use, immediately above it — the placement lesson from _NL_PAYLOAD_DIR, which was stripped from the entry script by an autoformat pass three times.

verification.command: per-file heredoc body hashing, before vs after
verification.evidence: THE decisive check for a file whose product is generated scripts. All 12 heredoc bodies were hashed in the pre-split file. After the split, 11 are byte-identical and the only one absent is the 224-line config-unlock body — which hashes to 1a5c67cfd0244101, exactly matching the payload file that now holds it. No new bodies appeared. Re-run after shfmt with the same result.
verification.note: An earlier run reported a spurious 302-line body and a spurious 9-line one. Both were artifacts of my own measurement: concatenating the libs joined one terminator to the next opener, and a `<<'EOF'` inside a comment I had written was parsed as a real heredoc. Measuring per-file and rewording the comment resolved both; neither was a change to the code.

verification.evidence: Two entries, both explained. +create_config_guard is the deliberate heredoc-to-payload change. -log is the trap this file is known for: log() was counted as top level because it appears at column 0 twice INSIDE generated scripts. It is not lost — it now sits at line 17 of the payload, which is where it always executed from.

verification.command: python3 line-multiset check against original (payload included)
verification.evidence: Two lines differ and both are the heredoc mechanics being replaced: `cat >"$unlock_script" <<'EOF'` and its `EOF` terminator, now a single `cat "$_MS_PAYLOAD_DIR/..."`. Every other code line is accounted for.

verification.command: diff of --help against the pre-split baseline
verification.evidence: Byte-identical, rc=0, re-checked after shfmt. `status` was not used as a baseline: it re-execs under sudo and fails on PATH when invoked by relative path.

shellcheck rc=0 with no suppression added; shfmt stable after one formatting pass; hyphenated-key canary clean. check_file_length reports 'all checked files are within 250 lines' — the campaign goal, with the payloads git-tracked so the gate genuinely sees them.

risks: `setup` is never executed under test: it writes systemd units, makes the config immutable and arms a real shutdown timer. Correctness rests on the heredoc-hash equality (which is what determines the generated scripts) plus the unchanged-function proof.
The deployed /usr/local/bin scripts are not rewritten by this commit and do not need to be — the split provably emits the same content.

verify_shell_split.sh cannot distinguish a heredoc-internal function from a top-level one. That is why the heredoc hashing exists; anyone re-verifying this file should treat the -log entry as expected rather than as a lost function.
rollback: git revert the commit; setup_midnight_shutdown.sh returns to one 1734-line file and lib/ms_*.sh plus the payload disappear.
Nothing to undo on the live system — no deployed file was written.
After rollback, re-run the heredoc hashing and confirm the combined fingerprint returns to dcf8be138f55dced.
